prompts.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: editorial hero photograph for a restrained Attio Mono clinical partnership marketing page.
Scene: a clinician and a clinical-programme administrator, both adults, in a quiet bright hospital education room, discussing a training programme at a small table. A closed notebook and an unobtrusive anatomical model provide medical-education context. Candid attentive conversation, not a posed handshake. Entirely fictional generic people and setting.
Style: polished natural editorial photography with realistic skin, hands and fabric; soft window daylight, warm white walls, neutral grey furniture and very restrained clinical blue/sage details. Calm professional mood, no dramatic advertising effect.
Composition: landscape 4:3, medium-wide eye-level view; keep both faces and the conversation in the central safe area for a modest responsive crop. No embedded copy.
Constraints: no identifiable institution, logos, signage, readable name badges, text, watermarks, readable screens, patient records or real patients. Do not depict or imply an existing GooCampus partnership.

Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: supporting editorial image in a clinical-education bento card on an Attio Mono marketing page.
Scene: a carefully composed but natural clinical teaching-room still life: a neutral anatomical model on a pale table beside a closed medical notebook and an unused stethoscope. Softly blurred bright teaching room in the background. Generic fictional setting, no people or patients.
Style: premium editorial photography, realistic ceramic/plastic/paper textures, soft side-window daylight, warm whites, pale stone and neutral greys with a small muted clinical-blue detail. Quiet uncluttered visual, no glossy stock-advertisement styling.
Composition: landscape 4:3, slightly elevated close-medium view, central teaching materials with generous breathing room. Suitable for a card without any text overlay.
Constraints: no logos, branding, readable text or labels, signage, monitors, patient information or watermark. Illustrative medical education only; no provider relationship implied.
